item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport class lacks a proper close() method that should be part of the Transport interface. Tests expect this method to exist and be callable.
item.contract: The SubprocessCLITransport class must implement a close() method that follows the same semantics as disconnect() and properly closes the underlying subprocess connection.

item.description: The receive_messages method in SubprocessCLITransport is not properly returning an AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]] that can be consumed by 'async for' loops. The method is missing proper async iteration protocol implementation.
item.contract: The receive_messages method must return a proper AsyncIterator that supports async iteration, allowing clients to consume messages with 'async for' syntax.

item.description: The SubprocessCLITransport class does not implement the complete Transport interface. Specifically, it's missing the close() method which is required by the abstract base class.
item.contract: The SubprocessCLITransport must fully implement all methods required by the Transport abstract base class, including connect, disconnect, send_request, receive_messages, and close.

item.description: The internal client's process_query method doesn't properly handle the transport's close method when exiting the context, which is needed for proper resource cleanup in streaming scenarios.
item.contract: The internal client must ensure proper cleanup of transport connections when processing queries, particularly in streaming mode.

item.description: The send_request method is not properly integrated with the streaming mode behavior. In streaming mode, the transport should be able to handle additional requests after initial connection.
item.contract: The send_request method must properly handle sending additional messages in streaming mode and work correctly with the async iteration mechanism.
